context_summary: F56 transforms the level editor into a Mario Maker 2-style tool. Currently the editor has a fixed camera, no enemy placement, and basic test-from-spawn only. This feature adds: (1) enemy palette with vacuum/pigeon/bee subtypes, (2) camera controls (WASD pan, scroll zoom), (3) test-from-cursor ('TESTAR DAQUI'), (4) seamless edit-play-edit cycle preserving editor state, (5) level resize (expand width/height). Medium-high scope but all changes are editor-side only, no gameplay or backend changes.

options_considered.description: Enhance existing editor incrementally: add enemy palette tab, camera controls, test-from-cursor, and resize to the current EditorScene3D/EditorUI/EditorWrapper architecture.
pros: Builds on solid existing editor codebase (EditorWrapper state, EditorUI palette tabs, EditorScene3D grid)
Enemy entities already exist in shared types and LevelSceneConverter — just need editor palette entry
Camera controls are independent of palette changes — can parallelize
Preserve editor state on test return is a sessionStorage pattern already used for clear-check
cons: EditorWrapper state grows larger — may need to extract to a Zustand store eventually
Camera controls require refactoring the fixed camera setup in Canvas

options_considered.description: Rewrite editor as a Zustand-driven system with separate EditorStore, decoupled camera, and plugin-based palette.
cons: Much larger scope — rewrites working code
High risk of regressions in existing editor functionality

rationale: Option A is the right approach. The existing editor architecture is solid and all additions are incremental. Enemy palette is trivial (copy existing entity palette pattern). Camera controls are a self-contained change to Canvas/EditorScene3D. Test-from-cursor extends the existing test flow. State preservation on return uses the sessionStorage pattern already proven for clear-check. Resize is a simple UI addition to change width/height bounds. Save the Zustand extraction for F57 (undo/redo) if needed.
